chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Barbarin grandparents and Haitian ancestry
summary: Danny describes his maternal grandparents Isadore Barbarin and Josephine and a Haitian great-grandmother who spoke French, Creole, Patois and Cajun.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And did you know your grandparents on both sides?
Yeah, sure. They lived to a ripe old age..
Well, what was your mother's parent's name?

My mother's father's name was Isadore John Barbarin. His wife, his maiden name was Josephine Auphidore(?). Her grandmother's mother had came from Haiti. She spoke French, she spoke Creole, she spoke Patois and Cajol(?). All of them is different versions of the French, all of them spoke by different people. French was spoken by the Whites. Cajol(?) was spoken by the White Cajuns who were living in the country -- from the Acadians. There was

a little deviation in all them versions [voizhins] of the French language. And she could speak all of them. Sometimes you could speak French, but you couldn't understand a Cajol, see, because they spoke French, bad French with a southern accent. See, French is a fluent language; you know, it flows.
In other words, your father's people came from Haiti...?
No, no. My grandmother's grandmother came from Haiti.
That's my mother's mother I'm speaking about. Josephine...
